Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:180168
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38186 of 2023

Applicant :- Vijay
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Shukla

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anjali Jaiswal,Dhirendra Kumar Verma Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
None appeared on behalf of the informant even in the revised call.
However, learned AGA, for the State, is present.

2. Heard Sri Pradeep Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA, for the State.
3. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.15 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366 and 376 (2)N IPC and Section 5J(2)/6, 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Fatehganj Poorvi, District Bareilly during pendency of the trial.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and one another under Section 366 IPC and according to the FIR, informant performed marriage of his daughter with one Sushil and after marriage when informant has taken her to his home then applicant with the help of his friend Ravi enticed her away.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that the daughter of the informant has also Vijay vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145678788/
1 taken jewellery along with her.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and actually marriage of the victim was performed with another person against her wishes and as she loved the applicant and,
therefore, even after marriage she had gone along with applicant and after performing marriage with him started living with him.
6.

He further submits that these facts are evident from both the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
7.

He further submits that as per the school record victim was around 17-1/2 years old girl but during investigation her ossification test could not be conducted and as she is more than 17 years old even as per her school record, therefore, precisely at this stage it cannot be said that she was below 18 years of age.
8.
He further submits that it is a case of love affair and applicant in the present matter is in jail since 2.7.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that as per school record victim was around 17 years old and, therefore, her consent is immaterial but he could not dispute the fact that in her both the statements recorded during investigation victim categorically stated that she according to her own wish had gone along with applicant and also performed marriage with him.
10. Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that even marriage of the victim had been performed with some other person against her wishes.

However, he further submits that applicant is having criminal history of Sections 394 and 411 IPC.
11.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. Although applicant is having criminal history of Sections 394 and 411 IPC and as per school record victim appears to be around 17 years old at the time of incident but from the record it reflects that the marriage of the victim was performed with some other person against her wishes and thereafter she had gone along with applicant and after performing marriage with him started living with him and she did not make any allegation against the applicant in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
The present case appears to be a case of love affair.

13. The law is settled that if otherwise case of bail is made out then merely on the basis of criminal history, bail should not be dismissed and further, bail application should not be dismissed either for punitive or preventive purposes.
14.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant-Vijay be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
